work.title: The First Part of Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

content.text: Sennet. Enter King, Gloucester and Exeter.

lines.text: Have you perused the letters from the Pope,
lines.plainText: Have you perused the letters from the Pope

lines.text: The Emperor, and the Earl of Armagnac?
lines.plainText: The Emperor and the Earl of Armagnac

lines.text: I have, my lord; and their intent is this:
lines.plainText: I have my lord and their intent is this

lines.text: They humbly sue unto your Excellence
lines.plainText: They humbly sue unto your Excellence

lines.text: To have a godly peace concluded of
lines.plainText: To have a godly peace concluded of

lines.text: Between the realms of England and of France.
lines.plainText: Between the realms of England and of France

lines.text: How doth your Grace affect their motion?
lines.plainText: How doth your Grace affect their motion

lines.text: Well, my good lord, and as the only means
lines.plainText: Well my good lord and as the only means

lines.text: To stop effusion of our Christian blood
lines.plainText: To stop effusion of our Christian blood

lines.text: And stablish quietness on every side.
lines.plainText: And stablish quietness on every side

lines.text: Ay, marry, uncle, for I always thought
lines.plainText: Ay marry uncle for I always thought

lines.text: It was both impious and unnatural
lines.plainText: It was both impious and unnatural

lines.text: That such immanity and bloody strife
lines.plainText: That such immanity and bloody strife

lines.text: Should reign among professors of one faith.
lines.plainText: Should reign among professors of one faith

lines.text: Beside, my lord, the sooner to effect
lines.plainText: Beside my lord the sooner to effect

lines.text: And surer bind this knot of amity,
lines.plainText: And surer bind this knot of amity

lines.text: The Earl of Armagnac, near knit to Charles,
lines.plainText: The Earl of Armagnac near knit to Charles

lines.text: A man of great authority in France,
lines.plainText: A man of great authority in France

lines.text: Proffers his only daughter to your Grace
lines.plainText: Proffers his only daughter to your Grace

lines.text: In marriage, with a large and sumptuous dowry.
lines.plainText: In marriage with a large and sumptuous dowry

lines.text: Marriage, uncle! Alas, my years are young!
lines.plainText: Marriage uncle Alas my years are young

lines.text: And fitter is my study and my books
lines.plainText: And fitter is my study and my books

lines.text: Than wanton dalliance with a paramour.
lines.plainText: Than wanton dalliance with a paramour

lines.text: Yet call th' ambassadors; and, as you please,
lines.plainText: Yet call th' ambassadors and as you please

lines.text: So let them have their answers every one.
lines.plainText: So let them have their answers every one

lines.text: I shall be well content with any choice
lines.plainText: I shall be well content with any choice

lines.text: Tends to God's glory and my country's weal.
lines.plainText: Tends to God's glory and my country's weal

content.text: Enter Winchester in Cardinal's habit, a Legate and two Ambassadors.

lines.text: What, is my Lord of Winchester install'd
lines.plainText: What is my Lord of Winchester install'd

lines.text: And call'd unto a cardinal's degree?
lines.plainText: And call'd unto a cardinal's degree

lines.text: Then I perceive that will be verified
lines.plainText: Then I perceive that will be verified

lines.text: Henry the Fifth did sometime prophesy:
lines.plainText: Henry the Fifth did sometime prophesy

lines.text: "If once he come to be a cardinal,
lines.plainText: If once he come to be a cardinal

lines.text: He'll make his cap co-equal with the crown."
lines.plainText: He'll make his cap coequal with the crown

lines.text: My Lords Ambassadors, your several suits
lines.plainText: My Lords Ambassadors your several suits

lines.text: Have been consider'd and debated on.
lines.plainText: Have been consider'd and debated on

lines.text: Your purpose is both good and reasonable;
lines.plainText: Your purpose is both good and reasonable

lines.text: And therefore are we certainly resolved
lines.plainText: And therefore are we certainly resolved

lines.text: To draw conditions of a friendly peace,
lines.plainText: To draw conditions of a friendly peace

lines.text: Which by my Lord of Winchester we mean
lines.plainText: Which by my Lord of Winchester we mean

lines.text: Shall be transported presently to France.
lines.plainText: Shall be transported presently to France

lines.text: And for the proffer of my lord your master,
lines.plainText: And for the proffer of my lord your master

lines.text: I have inform'd his Highness so at large,
lines.plainText: I have inform'd his Highness so at large

lines.text: As liking of the lady's virtuous gifts,
lines.plainText: As liking of the lady's virtuous gifts

lines.text: Her beauty and the value of her dower,
lines.plainText: Her beauty and the value of her dower

lines.text: He doth intend she shall be England's Queen.
lines.plainText: He doth intend she shall be England's Queen

lines.text: In argument and proof of which contract,
lines.plainText: In argument and proof of which contract

lines.text: Bear her this jewel, pledge of my affection.
lines.plainText: Bear her this jewel pledge of my affection

lines.text: And so, my Lord Protector, see them guarded
lines.plainText: And so my Lord Protector see them guarded

lines.text: And safely brought to Dover; where inshipp'd,
lines.plainText: And safely brought to Dover where inshipp'd

lines.text: Commit them to the fortune of the sea.
lines.plainText: Commit them to the fortune of the sea

lines.text: Stay my lord legate; you shall first receive
lines.plainText: Stay my lord legate you shall first receive

lines.text: The sum of money which I promised
lines.plainText: The sum of money which I promised

lines.text: Should be deliver'd to his Holiness
lines.plainText: Should be deliver'd to his Holiness

lines.text: For clothing me in these grave ornaments.
lines.plainText: For clothing me in these grave ornaments

lines.text: I will attend upon your lordship's leisure.
lines.plainText: I will attend upon your lordship's leisure

lines.text: [Aside.] Now Winchester will not submit, I trow,
lines.plainText: Aside Now Winchester will not submit I trow

lines.text: Or be inferior to the proudest peer.
lines.plainText: Or be inferior to the proudest peer

lines.text: Humphrey of Gloucester, thou shalt well perceive
lines.plainText: Humphrey of Gloucester thou shalt well perceive

lines.text: That neither in birth or for authority,
lines.plainText: That neither in birth or for authority

lines.text: The Bishop will be overborne by thee.
lines.plainText: The Bishop will be overborne by thee

lines.text: I'll either make thee stoop and bend thy knee,
lines.plainText: I'll either make thee stoop and bend thy knee

lines.text: Or sack this country with a mutiny.
lines.plainText: Or sack this country with a mutiny
